title: Native computation of the previous visit
statement: Let $M$ be a finite binary Turing machine, let $\tau$ be one of its work tapes, and let $m,T:\{0,1\}^*\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose the functions $x\mapsto 0^{m(x)}$ and $x\mapsto 1^{T(x)}$ are polynomial-time computable. Then the function sending $x$ to the optional-time code of the last time strictly before $T(x)$ at which tape $\tau$ occupied its position at time $T(x)$ on input $0^{m(x)}$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite binary Turing machine
$m,T$ map bit strings to natural numbers
replaced: For a source machine, work tape $\tau$, and polynomial-time producers of a reference length (as an all-false word) and a unary time, the function sending an input to the optional-time code of the public greatest strictly earlier visit to the currently scanned cell of $\tau$ is polynomial-time computable, with the canonical binary time encoding.
